entries.topicDescription: Diagnosing and improving app startup time, memory usage, and runtime performance.

tips.title: Baseline Profiles pre-compile hot code paths to speed up cold app startup
tips.content:
Without a Baseline Profile, the Android Runtime (ART) interprets and
JIT-compiles your app's code from scratch on every fresh install or app
update's first launches, which measurably slows down cold startup time
until the JIT has 'warmed up' the frequently-used code paths.

A Baseline Profile — a list of classes and methods known to be critical
to startup and common user flows — is shipped with the APK and lets ART
ahead-of-time compile those specific code paths at install time, giving
a faster cold start from the very first launch instead of only after
repeated JIT warm-up.

tips.title: Turn on StrictMode in debug builds to catch main-thread work
tips.content:
StrictMode is a developer tool that reports things that shouldn't happen on the main thread, such as disk reads and writes and network calls, and leaks like unclosed resources or leaked Activities. Turn it on only for debug builds, log the violations at first, and fix them as they show up, before they turn into dropped frames or ANRs in production.

Enable it as early as possible, in Application.onCreate, so startup work is covered too.

tips.title: Keep Application.onCreate light; defer initialization with App Startup
tips.content:
Everything you initialize in Application.onCreate (and in ContentProviders that libraries use to self-initialize) runs before the first screen can appear, so it directly slows cold start. Initialize only what the first screen needs, and defer or lazily create the rest.

The Jetpack App Startup library gives initialization a single, ordered entry point through Initializer classes with declared dependencies. You can also opt individual initializers out of automatic startup and trigger them on first use.

tips.title: Measure startup with Macrobenchmark instead of guessing
tips.content:
Startup time is easy to misjudge by feel or by a single run on your own phone. The Macrobenchmark library launches your release-like app repeatedly in a separate process and reports real timings, such as StartupTimingMetric for time-to-initial-display, with statistics across iterations.

Use CompilationMode to compare configurations, for example no pre-compilation against a Baseline Profile, so you can see what an optimization is actually worth.
